user_report: Auto Focus on a daytime terrestrial scene (antenna mast against bright sky, Main = ATR585M) fails. A normal camera's contrast autofocus would focus this scene. (Bundle reason field: 'Manual capture from UI (no note given)'.)
optical_setup: Main optical train, ATR585M (mono, 16-bit, 3840x2160), OnStep focuser, terrestrial scene; the three Main frames are NOT committed (large data stays local): local_test_data/56/frames/frame_0..2.fits, lossless uint16, made by scripts/slim_regression_frames.py from the diagnostic bundle -- see README.md

cases.name: added_defocus_lowers_the_score
cases.rationale: Known software transform: the mean of the three real Main frames is blurred by an exact (FFT) Gaussian of sigma 0/2/4/8/16/32 px -- strictly more defocus at every step -- and each level gets three fresh samples of the bundle's own measured sensor noise (sigma = std(frame_1 - frame_0)/sqrt(2) ~ 845 ADU, by hand). More defocus must give a strictly lower focus score; issue #56's acceptance criterion requires at least 5 % per coarse step from 4 px on (the 2->4, 4->8, 8->16, 16->32 steps), which the search's own 5 % improvement margin needs to see a slope. Before the fix the score was flat (< 20 % from 0 to 32 px) and non-monotone. Exercised by tests/regressions/test_issue_56_terrestrial_autofocus_regression.py (bespoke: the case builds a sweep, which the generic frame-pair driver cannot express).

cases.name: noise_alone_marks_no_tile_as_moving
cases.rationale: By construction: three frames of a constant (the real frame's median) plus independent Gaussian noise at the bundle's own measured sigma contain no moving content at all, so no tile may be rejected as moving. Before the fix the motion test compared a tile's change with its own std, which for a featureless tile is the noise (mean |diff| ~ 1.13 sigma > 0.5): 1760 of the bundle's 1980 tiles were rejected.

cases.name: replaced_tile_is_rejected_as_moving
cases.rationale: By construction: in the real frames, the 64x64 px sky tile at rows/cols 128..191 (exactly one production tile) is replaced in samples 1 and 2 by uniform random content of 5000..60000 ADU -- its content really changed -- so exactly one more tile than on the unmodified frames must be rejected as moving.

cases.name: score_independent_of_the_sample_set
cases.rationale: By construction: all three samples were taken at ONE focuser position, so every ordering, every subset and every duplicated re-read of them measures the same focus and must give the same score within the search's own 5 % improvement margin (BoundedFocusSearcher improvement_fraction = 0.05) -- otherwise sample noise alone can look like a focus step (issue #56 review F1: 27-58 % spread before).

cases.name: clipped_highlights_step_down
cases.rationale: Known software transform with a known optimum: the frames' clipped glints are set to K x full scale (K = 1, 3), the scene is defocused by a Gaussian of sigma = |position - 2500| / 50 px BEFORE clipping, scaled by the exposure and re-clipped; best focus is 2500 by construction. Driven through the real AutofocusController and BoundedFocusSearcher from 2500 +- 500, the run must step the exposure down and land within one coarse step (250) of 2500; with K = 10 (still clipping at the lowest exposure tried) or without exposure control it must report highlights_clipped, never SUCCESS (issue #56 review F3, contract amendment).
